reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number n with 3 ≤ n, every real number κ with 4 ≤ κ, and every real number ℓ with 0 ≤ ℓ, make the following definitions. Let j₀ = 0 be the first coordinate in Fin n = {0,…,n−1}. Let G = O(n) = {O ∈ ℝ^{n×n} : OᵀO = Iₙ} be the full real orthogonal group, including both determinant signs, with its inherited finite-matrix topology and Borel σ-algebra. Let μ be the normalized Haar measure on G, so μ(G) = 1. Identify E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with ℝⁿ, equipped with its Euclidean norm and canonical n-dimensional volume dx. Define U : G → ℝ by U(O) = O_{j₀j₀}, define a : G → ℝ by a(O) = κ + 1 + 4ℓ − (κ − 1)U(O), and let p = (n as a real number)/2 ∈ ℝ. For notation in the conclusions, write B(O) = ((κ + 1)/2)Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).

Then all of the following conclusions hold simultaneously:
(1) For every O ∈ G, the real function x ↦ exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) on E is absolutely Bochner L¹-integrable with respect to dx.
(2) The real function O ↦ det(O) sqrt(det(B(O))) [∫_E exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) dx] is absolutely Bochner L¹-integrable with respect to μ.
(3) The real function O ↦ ((sqrt(κ) + 1)U(O) − (sqrt(κ) − 1))/a(O)^p is absolutely Bochner L¹-integrable with respect to μ.
(4) The following exact identity holds for the indicated iterated integral:

[∫_G det(O) sqrt(det(((κ + 1)/2)Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ))) [∫_E exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) dx] dμ(O)]/(2π)^p
= [(-1)^(n−1) (sqrt(κ) − 1)^(n−1)/2^p] [∫_G ((sqrt(κ) + 1)U(O) − (sqrt(κ) − 1))/a(O)^p dμ(O)].

Every square root denotes the nonnegative real square root. Every power with exponent p uses the real exponent p = n/2, including when n is odd; each power with exponent n−1 has the natural exponent n−1. The inner integral is over x and canonical volume, and every outer integral is over the whole group G with the same normalized Haar measure μ. There are no hypotheses of spatial or outer integrability: the three L¹ assertions above are part of the conclusion.
objects: j₀ is the zero-based coordinate 0 in Fin n. G is the full orthogonal group O(n). μ is its actual normalized Haar probability measure. E is the real n-dimensional Euclidean space with canonical volume dx. U(O)=O_{00}; a(O)=κ+1+4ℓ−(κ−1)U(O); p=(n:ℝ)/2. The notational matrix B(O)=((κ+1)/2)Iₙ−((κ−1)/4)(O+Oᵀ) expands the determinant argument literally.
domains: n∈ℕ with n≥3; κ∈ℝ with κ≥4; ℓ∈ℝ with ℓ≥0. O ranges over all real n×n orthogonal matrices, with finite-matrix topology and Borel σ-algebra, including determinant +1 and −1. x ranges over E=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with Euclidean norm and n-dimensional volume. U,a:G→ℝ and p∈ℝ.
quantifiers: For every n∈ℕ, if 3≤n, then for every κ∈ℝ, if 4≤κ, then for every ℓ∈ℝ, if 0≤ℓ, the four conjunctive conclusions hold for the displayed lets. The first conclusion has an additional universal quantifier over every O∈G. Integration binds x in E and O in G in the respective inner and outer integrals.
assumptions: The only numerical hypotheses are 3≤n, 4≤κ, and 0≤ℓ. The definitions supply the full orthogonal group, normalized Haar probability measure, Euclidean norm and canonical volume. No integrability hypothesis, arbitrary measure, restriction to special orthogonal matrices, conditional law, or additional free parameter occurs.
conclusion: For every O, x↦exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) lies in L¹(dx); O↦det(O)sqrt(det B(O))∫_E exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4)dx lies in L¹(μ); and O↦((sqrtκ+1)U(O)−(sqrtκ−1))/a(O)^p lies in L¹(μ). The exact iterated-integral identity is (∫_G det(O)sqrt(det B(O))(∫_E exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4)dx)dμ(O))/(2π)^p = ((−1)^(n−1)(sqrtκ−1)^(n−1)/2^p)∫_G ((sqrtκ+1)U(O)−(sqrtκ−1))/a(O)^p dμ(O). All three L¹ statements mean absolute Bochner integrability.
scopes: All four conclusions are conjoined under the same choices of n,κ,ℓ and literal lets j₀,U,a,p. B is only explanatory notation for the displayed matrix. The spatial integral binds x and uses volume; its value depends on the outer O. Both group integrals and both group L¹ statements use μ on the whole group. sqrt applies to det B(O), while det(O) multiplies outside that square root. Division by (2π)^p applies to the entire left outer integral. The entire right outer integral is multiplied by (−1)^(n−1)(sqrtκ−1)^(n−1)/2^p.
constant_dependencies: p is the real number n/2, not natural-number division. The left normalizer is (2π)^(n/2); the right scalar is (−1)^(n−1)(sqrtκ−1)^(n−1)/2^(n/2), depending only on n and κ. The exponent of the spatial exponential is exactly −a(O)‖x‖²/4, and a(O)=κ+1+4ℓ−(κ−1)U(O). The determinant matrix coefficients are exactly (κ+1)/2 and (κ−1)/4. The right numerator is exactly (sqrtκ+1)U(O)−(sqrtκ−1), and its denominator is a(O)^(n/2). ℓ occurs through a only. No unspecified or existential constant occurs.
